faq.a: Abdelhadi represents Arabic عبد الهادي, meaning servant of al-Hādī (“the Guide”).

faq.q: What is the origin of Abdelhadi?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and الهادي.
Yes. The underlying compound is عبد الهادي (ʿAbd al-Hādī).

faq.q: What is the root of Abdelhadi?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د, while الهادي is related to ه د ي, associated with guidance.
Abdelhadi is a traditional Muslim name because it contains al-Hādī, a divine name in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abdelhadi as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.a: In Urdu, عبدالہادی means servant of al-Hādī, understood as the Guide.
The supplied “ab-del-ha-di” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.a: The record classifies Abdelhadi as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
